title: Where the watering beam plays in the cold open
question: You asked for the watering beam loop as a shot when the player first watches the neighbour water through the fence. Your own revision of the cold open made it never take control away: the fence made the restriction spatial instead of a camera cut. A full-screen shot in the middle of it would be the game's first cut-in during play. The loop itself is a good pick, water hitting the soil at close range; the question is where it plays.
why_now: The cold open is the first thing a new player meets, and this decides whether the game ever cuts away during play.

options.label: An inset card while she keeps control (Recommended)
options.detail: The shot plays in a corner over the fence while the neighbour waters and the player stays free in her own yard. Keeps the fence's promise and still shows the water at close range.

options.label: The overnight after her own first watering
options.detail: The shot moves to the sleep after the first day she waters a tile herself, under the overnight rule (P-15). It becomes a reward for doing it rather than a demonstration of watching it.

options.label: A full-screen shot during the neighbour's watering
options.detail: The game cuts away for the loop, overruling the cold open's rule for this one moment, knowingly. The most legible close-up, at the cost of the first cut-in during play.
